caution_words: A standing caution, printed on purpose: a dozen weekly windows cannot prove skill either way. A group can look hot for twelve weeks by luck alone, and a good group can look cold the same way. That is why no group's state is ever called proven on this page, however its chances move.

explanation.body: Its forecast takes this form: probability, over next 21 sessions, weekly (Monday). It is graded on a score that rewards probabilities that land close to what actually happens. It would be ended if after 12 windows, pooled Brier is no better than climatology (each forecaster's trailing rate, unchanged), and the engine is demoted to the Graveyard with its record intact. It counts as proven at 12 windows.
explanation.summary: Every Monday, stake a chance on whether each tracked group of forecasters is about to have a better next 21 trading days than its own last 126, using its own report card alone.

how_words: Four readings, all from the group's own grades: the change between the first and second halves of its last 126 trading days; whether its right calls bunch together in runs or scatter; how its own stated scores compare with its results, where its record carries a score at all (today only the Board gate's record does); and how its number of calls in the latest 21 trading days compares with the 21 before those. Those readings nudge the group's own past rate up or down by a small amount written down in advance, never by more than 15 points, and the chance is then counted exactly from that nudged rate and the number of calls the group is expected to make. Beside every chance sits the no-change rival: the chance if the group's past rate simply carries on, computed the same way with no nudge.
idea_words: Every forecaster on this site keeps a report card: the share of its past calls that turned out right. This page forecasts the report card itself. Each Monday it asks, for each group of forecasters: what is the chance that the group's next 21 trading days go better than its own last 126 trading days did? The chance is built only from that group's own report card: whether its recent grades are improving, whether its right calls come in runs, whether its stated scores line up with how often it is right, and whether it is making more or fewer calls than usual. No price of any stock or index is used, at all.
kill_words: After 12 graded weekly windows, if this page's chances have not scored better than the no-change rival's chances over the same windows, this page retires and its record stays up, exactly as it stands.

self_test.words: The whole path is exercised on every refresh with made-up report cards in a throwaway record: a group whose right calls bunch in a hot run gets a higher chance than its no-change rival, a fading group gets a lower one, a coin-flip group stays within 5 points of its rival, and a group that was right every time is handled without error. Each made-up window is then graded at its close, beside its rival, in the throwaway record only: nothing made up ever reaches the public record or this page's figures.
